disease_label_per_paper: Henoch-Schonlein purpura presenting as upper gastrointestinal bleed in an adult patient
presentation_summary: Previously healthy 18-year-old male presented with one day of bloody vomitus, fever/chills by history, central constant dull abdominal pain rated 6/10, and non-bloody diarrhea.
Two weeks before presentation he had rhinorrhea and sore throat; one week after symptom onset he developed bilateral knee and ankle arthralgias that limited weight bearing and ambulation.
The arthralgias were followed by painless purpuric rash starting at the left ankle and extending proximally and bilaterally.
In the emergency department he was afebrile and hemodynamically stable; examination showed palpable, purpuric, non-blanchable rash involving both lower extremities.
Admission labs showed WBC 10.8 x10^9/L, hemoglobin 15.8 g/dL, platelets 243 x10^9/L, creatinine 0.97 mg/dL, AST 47 U/L, ALT 58 U/L, and CRP 4.8 mg/L.
Urine dipstick was positive for trace hemoglobin and +2 proteinuria; ANA, ANCA, C3, C4, HIV screen, hepatitis panel, PT, aPTT, and blood cultures were within normal limits or negative.
Chest X-ray, abdominal ultrasound, and CT abdomen/pelvis were unremarkable.
Upper endoscopy showed non-bleeding erosive gastropathy, duodenal bulb erosions, and erosive mucosal changes.
Skin biopsy of the left leg showed leukocytoclastic vasculitis with IgA and fibrin deposition in superficial dermal vessel walls.

He received IV methylprednisolone 500 mg daily for three days, additional outpatient methylprednisolone infusions, steroid taper, and mycophenolate mofetil for incomplete response; abdominal pain and diarrhea resolved and he remained in remission.

clinical_course.event: Presented with hematemesis, abdominal pain, diarrhea, arthralgia history, and lower-extremity palpable purpura.
Skin biopsy and endoscopic findings supported IgA vasculitis with GI involvement.
Steroids were continued outpatient; mycophenolate was added for incomplete clinical response.
Symptoms improved significantly and he no longer had abdominal pain or diarrhea.

outcome.source_text_value: His symptoms improved significantly, and he no longer complained of abdominal pain or diarrhea; regimen tapered gradually and he has since remained in remission.
